label: Positions, functional roles, archetypes and skills
definition: The agent layer of the ontology. Nominal positions (1-5) are kept separate from functional roles (what a player actually does in a scheme) and from archetypes (the reproducible skill bundle that makes a player suited to a role).

nodes.label: Guard
nodes.definition: Perimeter ball-handling group (1-2). Initiates offence, defends the ball.

nodes.label: Wing
nodes.definition: Perimeter/forward hybrid group (2-3). Connect the arc and the paint, defends the best perimeter scorer.

nodes.label: Big
nodes.definition: Frontcourt group (4-5). Screens, rolls, protects the rim, controls the glass.

nodes.label: Point Guard
nodes.definition: The nominal '1'. Traditionally the primary initiator: brings the ball up, calls the action, sets the table.

key: Sets the tempo and the first call of the possession
In modern systems the '1' is a label, not a licence: any player may initiate

nodes.label: Shooting Guard
nodes.definition: The nominal '2'. Historically the scoring guard; today usually a movement shooter or a secondary creator.

nodes.label: Small Forward
nodes.definition: The nominal '3'. The most interchangeable position: must be able to shoot, switch on defence and attack a closeout.

nodes.label: Power Forward
nodes.definition: The nominal '4'. The modern 'stretch four' spaces the floor; the classic four screened, rebounded and scored inside.

props.note: The most archetype-volatile position in the modern game: stretch four vs small-ball four changes the whole scheme.

nodes.label: Center
nodes.definition: The nominal '5'. Anchors the rim defensively and screens/rolls offensively; in hub systems he is the primary passer.

nodes.label: Initiator
nodes.definition: The player who starts the offence: makes the first call, gets the ball to the action.

nodes.label: Ball Handler
nodes.definition: The player with the ball in a ball-screen or dribble-hand-off action. Reads the coverage and chooses the branch.

nodes.label: Screener
nodes.definition: The player who sets the screen: on-ball (ball screen), or off-ball (down, flare, pin, stagger).

nodes.label: Roll Man
nodes.definition: The screener after the screen: attacks the rim (roll), floats to the elbow (short roll) or spaces to the arc (pop).

nodes.label: Pop Man
nodes.definition: A screener whose second action is to space beyond the arc instead of rolling, dragging the rim protector out of the paint.

nodes.label: Hub
nodes.definition: The player stationed at the elbow, high post or short roll who receives against a rotating defence and re-distributes.

nodes.label: Connector
nodes.definition: The secondary creator who turns a first advantage into a second one: dribble hand-offs, quick swings, closeout attacks.

nodes.label: Secondary Creator
nodes.definition: The second ball-handling option: runs the second action when the first is taken away, and punishes a defence that loads up on the primary creator.

nodes.label: Spot-Up Shooter
nodes.definition: A floor spacer who occupies a defined spot (usually a corner) and punishes help with a catch-and-shoot three.

nodes.label: Off-Ball Mover
nodes.definition: A player who relocates, cuts and screens without the ball to stress the defence's attention and rules.

nodes.label: Stretch Big
nodes.definition: A frontcourt player who must be guarded beyond the arc, which removes his defender from the rim.

nodes.label: Rim Runner
nodes.definition: The player who sprints the floor in transition to pressure the rim before the defence can set.

nodes.label: On-Ball Defender
nodes.definition: Point-of-attack defender: contains the ball, navigates screens, executes the coverage.

nodes.label: Help Defender (Nail / Low Man)
nodes.definition: The off-ball defender who occupies the help position: the nail (free-throw line) on the ball side or the weak-side low man on the split line.

nodes.label: Rim Protector
nodes.definition: The last line: contests at the rim, goes vertical, and deters penetration simply by being there.

nodes.label: Perimeter Stopper
nodes.definition: The defender assigned to the opponent's best perimeter scorer across positions.

nodes.label: Switchable Defender
nodes.definition: A defender who can hold up after a switch against both bigger and smaller players, enabling switch-all schemes.

nodes.label: Rebounder / Boxer-Out
nodes.definition: Responsible for ending the possession on the defensive glass: find a body, then go get the ball.

nodes.label: Ball handling
nodes.definition: Ability to advance, protect and manipulate the ball against pressure.

nodes.label: Passing vision
nodes.definition: Ability to read a rotating defence and deliver the ball on time and on target.

nodes.label: Short-roll decision making
nodes.definition: Processing a 4-on-3 from the elbow: shoot, pass or attack.

nodes.label: Three-point shooting
nodes.definition: Range and accuracy beyond the arc, off the catch or off the dribble.

nodes.label: Catch-and-shoot
nodes.definition: Footwork and release speed to shoot immediately on the catch.

nodes.label: Rim finishing
nodes.definition: Converting at the rim through contact, with either hand, off either foot.

nodes.label: Vertical spacing
nodes.definition: Lob radius and leaping threat that turns a roll into a rim attempt.

nodes.label: Screen setting
nodes.definition: Angle, timing, legality and physicality of screening.

nodes.label: Off-ball movement
nodes.definition: Cutting, relocating and screening away to create without the ball.

nodes.label: Post footwork
nodes.definition: Sealing, duck-ins, pivots and counters from the block.

nodes.label: Screen navigation
nodes.definition: Defensive ability to get over, under or through screens and stay attached.

nodes.label: Lateral quickness
nodes.definition: Ability to stay in front of the ball and to close out under control.

nodes.label: Switch versatility
nodes.definition: Defending multiple positions credibly after a switch.

nodes.label: Help-side timing
nodes.definition: Arriving in the help position on the pass, not after it, and recovering in time.

nodes.label: Length
nodes.definition: Wingspan and standing reach that shrink passing lanes and contest shots.

nodes.label: Rebounding
nodes.definition: Boxing out, tracking the ball and finishing the possession.

nodes.label: Pick-and-Roll Initiator (Helmsman)
nodes.definition: High-usage ball-screen operator who scores and passes out of the action and dictates the coverage the defence must choose.

nodes.label: Pull-Up Shooter
nodes.definition: A ball handler who can stop on a dime and shoot off the dribble over a screen, punishing any coverage that goes under or drops.

nodes.label: Rim-Running Big
nodes.definition: Screens, then sprints to the rim with a wide catch radius; his value is the vertical pressure he puts on the paint even when he never touches the ball.

nodes.label: Roll-and-Pop Big (Stretch 5)
nodes.definition: A screener who pops to the arc after screening, dragging the rim protector away from the basket and emptying the paint for drivers.

nodes.label: Short-Roll Passer
nodes.definition: Catches the ball at the elbow against a collapsed defence and plays 4-on-3: the antidote to blitz and trap coverages.

nodes.label: Hub Playmaker
nodes.definition: A big who receives at the elbow or high post and runs the offence from there, reading the back line of the defence and delivering to cutters and shooters.

nodes.label: Spacing Big (Stretch 4)
nodes.definition: A frontcourt player whose shooting forces a rim protector to defend on the perimeter, opening the lane and the roll.

nodes.label: Off-Ball Sharpshooter
nodes.definition: A movement shooter who runs the defence through screens, relocates to the corner, and punishes any late rotation.

nodes.label: 3-and-D Wing
nodes.definition: A wing who can guard the best perimeter player and still space the floor in the corner; the connective tissue of modern lineups.

nodes.label: Slasher
nodes.definition: An attacker who beats a closeout and gets to the rim, forcing the defence to collapse and generating kick-outs.

nodes.label: Secondary Creator
nodes.definition: A guard or wing who can run a second action off the primary advantage: hand-offs, pick-and-rolls and closeout attacks.

nodes.label: Post Scorer
nodes.definition: Establishes position on the block, seals, and scores or doubles-and-passes; the mismatch punishment for switch-heavy defences.

nodes.label: Rim Protector
nodes.definition: Anchors the back line: contests at the rim, deters drives and erases the roll. His presence is the reason drop coverage exists.

nodes.label: Drop-Coverage Big
nodes.definition: A defensive anchor who sinks to the level of the free-throw line in ball screens to protect the rim and concede the pull-up.

nodes.label: Perimeter Stopper
nodes.definition: Point-of-attack defender who navigates screens, fights over the top and takes away the initiator's comfort.

nodes.label: Switchable Defender
nodes.definition: Defends 1 through 5 credibly; the enabler of switch-all schemes that take away the pass out of the pick-and-roll.

nodes.label: Help-Side Roamer
nodes.definition: An off-ball defender who plays the passing lanes and the nail, generating deflections and early offence.

nodes.label: Aggressive Blitzer
nodes.definition: A screen defender who attacks the ball handler with a double-team, betting that the offence cannot pass out of it on time.
